sections.changelog:
Added

  • **The parts for the plain model come first, the variants after.** "battery iPhone 13" matches the batteries of four different phones — the 13, the 13 mini, the 13 Pro and the 13 Pro Max — and every one of them clears the same number of words, so the order inside that tier fell to relevance and sales and mixed them. Measured on a 14 700-product catalogue, the plain model held places 1, 4, 8, 11 and 16 out of 17. A title is now charged for every model modifier standing directly behind the model number that the query never named, and equally for a modifier the query did name and the title lacks — so the same search leads with the plain 13, and "13 pro max" leads with the Pro Max. Both spellings are read, latin and cyrillic: "12 мини" lifts the mini, which it could not do before, because "макс" and "плюс" have no transliteration the catalogue carries and the words were simply invisible. The two spellings that hide a modifier inside the number are pulled apart — glued ("S20FE", 18 titles of the 78 carrying that model) and signed ("J6+", 58 titles across the catalogue) — while a part number like "68+E" is deliberately left alone. Nothing is filtered: a variant that does not match the wording stays on the page, one tier lower. A query naming no model is untouched, as is a catalogue that does not name models at all. Costs 0.26–1.31 ms against a 193–500 ms search. New setting under Relevance, on by default.

Fixed

  • **A sold-out product no longer climbs back up when the results are re-sorted.** The ranking query puts stock ahead of everything else, but the flag never left the query: the passes that reorder results in PHP could not see it, so any one of them reshuffling a tier handed a sold-out product a place the query had taken away from it. Measured on a 14 700-product catalogue with 238 sold-out products: one of them sat last in "battery iPhone 13" and moved up to fifth, above twelve products in stock. The flag now travels with every row and all three passes sort on it first, exactly as the query does. Only affects the "move to the end" stock mode, which is the only one where sold-out products are shown at all.
